transcript: The internet's rulebook spent ten years arguing about three letters. In two thousand, a company asked ICANN, the group that approves domain endings, for a new one: [short pause] dot x x x. The pitch was simple. Put adult websites in one labeled neighborhood. Easy to find, easy to filter. ICANN said no. The company came back in two thousand four. This time, ICANN leaned yes. Then the letters poured in. Conservative groups said it would make porn look official. Governments raised concerns too. So ICANN flipped, and rejected it again in two thousand seven. Here's the twist. [short pause] The adult industry hated it too. Porn sites feared a digital ghetto. One switch, and governments could block the whole street. The company fought back with an independent review, and in twenty-ten the panel sided with it. In twenty-eleven, it finally launched. Brands and universities paid to lock their names away. Ten years. Three letters. Everyone mad. [deadpan] Sounds like the internet.
